A 1,500-day streak, and still silence. What apps actually measure

A 1,500-day streak in an app, and silence in conversation. A streak counts taps, not speaking. Here is what you should measure instead.

Published November 24, 2026 · 6 min read · Sławomir Onyszko

A scene I see in forums all the time: "My partner has a 1,500-day streak in an app and wonders why she still doesn't speak."

She spent more than four years on daily practice. Four years of tapping continue and listening to the sound of the correct answer. Then she has to order coffee in Spanish or say something in a meeting, and silence arrives.

If you have a long streak and the same result, keep reading. There is one question nobody asks: what does your streak actually count?

What a streak counts

Look at a typical app lesson:

  • You see a sentence and choose the translation from four options.
  • You hear a word and tap the right one.
  • You fill in a gap by tapping one of three ready-made fragments.
  • You listen to a recording and mark what you heard.

Now the question: at what moment did you have to build your own sentence and say it out loud? Without hints, without options, under time pressure?

That moment almost never comes. The streak counts your presence and your taps. It counts how many times you recognized the right answer. It almost never counts a sentence that came out of your mouth.

That does not mean the app is useless. It gives you words and a habit. But it does not give you speaking. Speaking needs a different exercise: you have to say something of your own, then hear what was wrong.

Imagine a lesson about the past tense. The app shows Ayer ___ al mercado and three answers: fui, voy, ir. You tap fui and get points. But you never have to say Ayer fui al mercado out loud. You do not have to build a sentence about your own day. You recognized the correct form. You did not say it.

Attendance is not a grade

In school there were two different things people confuse: attendance and knowledge. You can have perfect attendance and know nothing. Nobody passes an exam for attendance.

In apps the same mechanism works in the other direction. A streak is an attendance log. It shows only presence, so it starts pretending to be a grade. It grows, the streak almost never breaks, the app level goes up. The skill you cared about is not measured.

It is like keeping an attendance log at the gym and never lifting the barbell. After a year you have a beautiful notebook with dates and the same strength as day one. Nobody checks whether the muscles grew. Everyone looks at attendance.

Why it looks like progress

A streak is the easiest metric to notice, so it looks like progress. Progress in speaking is invisible for months. You do not feel words arriving when you need them. So your brain grabs what can be counted: days, points, levels.

The app gives you numbers that always grow, and that is hard to resist. They quietly replace the question that really matters. Not did I do a lesson today, but can I say more than I could a year ago.

This is not an accusation against you. It is an accusation against the metric. The metric measures what is easy to count, not what matters.

There is another trap. A streak gives you a sense of control. Every day you see that you did something, and that feeling is pleasant. The brain likes rewards that arrive quickly. Speaking rewards you later, so it is easy to postpone. That is why it is so hard to swap taps for speaking, even when you know it works.

Same result, same method

This is not a story about one unlucky person. Go to a language-learning forum and you will see the same pattern:

  • "Half an hour a day for six months, the course is finished, and I still don't speak."
  • "It is a game I play, and I feel productive even though I can't say anything."

Notice one thing: the people in these threads blame the method, not their talent or age. They blame the mechanism. And they are right. Recognition training does not build speaking. It did not build it for you either. It was not a lack of motivation. You had enough motivation for 1,500 days.

That matters because it changes the question. The question changes from what is wrong with me to what is missing from the method.

What happens if you only keep the streak

The streak grows while speaking stands still. Every month adds three things:

  • The habit of silence gets stronger. The routine stays the same: tap, tap, tap, without a single sentence out loud.
  • Real opportunities do not wait: a job interview, a promotion, a move, a conversation with your partner's family.
  • Passive Spanish, the Spanish you understand but do not speak, fades without upkeep. The Spanish you have today is not a guarantee that it will be the same next year.

This is not about quitting the app. It is about no longer treating the streak as proof that you can speak. The streak says you showed up. It does not say what stayed in your head.

What a real metric would count

If you switched from checking off lessons to speaking practice tomorrow, the metrics would look different:

  • How many sentences you said today in your own words.
  • How many mistakes you made and how many were corrected.
  • What you remembered after 3 days, not in the same minute.

Those are three numbers. None of them counts taps. And each one says more about whether you can speak than the longest streak.

You do not need a complicated journal. A note on your phone or a piece of paper is enough. After a session, write three things: how many sentences you said out loud, how many corrections you understood and what you remembered from the previous week. After a month you can look back at a line the app never showed you.

Today the 3 sentences matter

Open your app and look at the streak. Ask it one question: what exactly did I count today? Answer honestly. You do not have to do it perfectly. 3 sentences and 1 missing word are enough.

Then, without any app, say 3 sentences out loud about what you did today, what you will do tomorrow and what makes you happy. Say them in Spanish. For example: Hoy terminé un informe. Mañana tengo un día libre. Estoy contento por eso. 3 sentences nobody hears, so a mistake costs nothing.

That will be the first day of a practice record that counts something more. Do the same tomorrow and the day after. After 3 days you will have your own data: 3 sessions, 3 recordings, and a note about what was hard. That is not proof yet. It is a first record. Three sentences will not fix all of the speaking. It is a first step, not the whole method.
